title: Greywater Bay Rising
premise: Lior Reyes, a night-shift dispatcher for Greywater Bay Taxi, has built her reputation on closing every case she takes — until a drowned woman washes up wearing clothes stolen from Lior's own closet, and the only witness is a man who swears he saw Lior herself near the water. Digging for an alibi drags her back to the Marisol case, the missing-girl investigation her adoptive family declared closed seven years ago, just before they adopted her. As the anniversary dinner of that closure approaches, Lior discovers the drowned woman was the last person to see Marisol alive, and that her new family's loyalty was purchased with a lie. In the end, Lior must choose between protecting the found family who saved her and exposing the truth: that her adoptive father covered up Marisol's accidental death, and the drowned woman was killed by his old partner to keep it buried.
about_author: Ulyana Ashgrove is a former emergency dispatcher from a fog-bound coastal town who writes mysteries steeped in radio static, salt air, and the secrets small cities keep. She lives with her partner and an opinionated gull she refuses to name.

chapters.title: Static on Line Three
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A routine night shift at Greywater Bay Taxi dispatch; Lior closes a runaway-bride fare with characteristic flair, establishing her pride in never losing a case. A strange call comes in — breathing, then silence, from a number tied to the marina. Emotional beat: confident competence shadowed by unease.

chapters.title: The Woman in My Clothes
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Police wake her at dawn: a body pulled from Greywater Bay wears Lior's own missing green coat and scarf. Detective Imara Voss treats her as suspect first, witness second. Emotional beat: violation and disbelief as her safe, ordered life cracks open.

chapters.title: Everyone Swore It Was Closed
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Pressed for an alibi, Lior realizes the murder date falls on the eve of the Marisol anniversary dinner — the case her adoptive family closed seven years ago. Flashback fragments of the night she was taken in. Emotional beat: dread of reopening what her family buried.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Saw Me
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The sole witness, dockhand Teo Brandt, insists he saw someone in the green coat at the pier at midnight — and describes Lior's walk. Voss notes inconsistencies but can't dismiss him. Emotional beat: cold procedural tension; the noose tightening around an innocent woman.

chapters.title: Dinner at the Hallorans'
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior attends her adoptive family's pre-anniversary dinner and probes gently about Marisol; her father Elias shuts down hard, her mother Ruth over-smiles, brother Devi warns her off. Emotional beat: love laced with fear — the family's loyalty feels like a wall.

chapters.title: Fare Records Don't Lie
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Using dispatch archives, Lior reconstructs cab activity the night of the drowning and finds a fare from the marina paid in cash by a man whose description matches Elias's former business partner, Callum Wray. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: What Teo Wouldn't Say
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. Teo admits to himself (and later Lior) that he lied about the time of the sighting — he was poaching crab pots and shifted his story to protect himself. He saw two figures, not one. Emotional beat: guilt; a flawed man deciding to do one right thing.

chapters.title: The Green Coat
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior traces how her coat was stolen — a break-in timed while she slept, meaning the killer knew her schedule, her home, her habits. Only a handful of people could. Emotional beat: paranoia invading the one place that felt safe.

chapters.title: Marisol's Last Fare
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Seven years ago, Marisol Vance took a taxi the night she vanished — and the driver's log page is torn out. Lior finds the retired driver, who confesses he dropped her at the Wray boathouse and was paid to forget. Emotional beat: the past reaching through the present.

chapters.title: Devi Knows Something
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Devi confronts Lior, begging her to stop before the dinner; he reveals he was the one who found Marisol's body as a teen and was made to swear silence by Elias. Emotional beat: sibling love weaponized by secrecy; Devi's shame finally surfacing.

chapters.title: Closed Case, Open Wound
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior pulls the original Marisol file: ruled an accident, signed off by a coroner since discredited, with Callum Wray listed as the last interviewee. The drowned woman, she learns, was Marisol's cousin who'd recently come asking questions. Emotional beat: the two cases locking together like bones.

chapters.title: Ruth's Quiet Hours
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth has known more than she ever admitted — she found Elias burning papers years ago and chose the family over the truth. Watching Lior dig, she wavers between protecting her husband and her daughter. Emotional beat: a mother's divided heart.

chapters.title: Midnight at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior and Teo stake out Wray's boathouse and catch him burning boxes; inside are Marisol's belongings and the drowned woman's phone. They're spotted and flee through the marsh. Emotional beat: terror and adrenaline; the case turns dangerous.

chapters.title: Voss Crosses the Line
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss, pressured to charge Lior before the anniversary, quietly verifies the coat theft timeline and realizes the frame job is real. She risks her career by sharing the file with Lior. Emotional beat: grudging alliance; duty bending toward truth.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Toast
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At the anniversary dinner celebrating the closed case, Lior stands to speak and instead asks Elias directly whether Callum Wray was there the night Marisol died. The room goes silent; Elias says yes — and that it was an accident he helped hide. Emotional beat: shattering of the family myth.

chapters.title: Confession and Cover-Up
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias recounts the truth: Marisol died falling from the boathouse loft during a confrontation with Wray over money; Elias buried it to save Devi, who'd witnessed it, from trauma and suspicion. But he swears the recent drowning wasn't him. Emotional beat: grief, guilt, and a father's terrible arithmetic.

chapters.title: One Case Left Open
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. If Elias didn't kill the cousin, Wray did — and Wray knows the family is cracking. Lior realizes the stolen-coat frame was designed to pin everything on her if anyone got close. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into purpose; she will close this case or die trying.

chapters.title: The Trap on Channel Nine
chapters.summary: Lior and Voss's POVs alternating. They bait Wray using dispatch channels, leaking that the boathouse evidence survived. Wray takes it, planning to burn the marsh shed where Lior stashed copies. Emotional beat: hunter becoming hunted; quiet, coiled suspense.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Climax at the marsh shed: Wray comes to destroy the evidence and finds Lior waiting; Teo and Voss close in, but Wray takes Lior to the water's edge. Devi arrives and testifies aloud, breaking his seven-year silence as sirens flood the shore. Emotional beat: raw courage; truth spoken at knifepoint.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings Back
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Wray is arrested; the Marisol case is officially reopened and reclassified. Voss clears Lior formally and offers her a consultant role she isn't sure she wants. Emotional beat: exhausted vindication; justice arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: Dinner, Rewritten
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The family gathers again — not to toast a lie but to mourn Marisol properly. Elias accepts consequences; Devi begins therapy; Ruth holds them all together. Lior isn't sure she can forgive yet, but she stays. Emotional beat: fragile reconciliation; found family tested and remade.

chapters.title: Last Call of the Night Shift
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Weeks later, back on dispatch, Lior takes a call from a scared girl running from something and talks her safely home — then pins a new card above her desk: every case closes, eventually. The green coat, returned from evidence, hangs by the door. Emotional beat: quiet peace; love chosen over duty, truth over comfort.
